L00004: BLADE: Benchmarking Language Model Agents for Data-Driven Science L00005:

L00006: L00007: ![PyPI - Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/blade-bench) L00008: ![PyPI - Python Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/blade-bench) L00009: [![Website](https://img.shields.io/website?url=https%3A%2F%2Fblade-bench.github.io%2F&up_message=online&style=flat)](https://blade-bench.github.io/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/Code%20License-Apache%202.0-red.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) L00010: [![Data License](https://img.shields.io/badge/Data%20License-ODC%20Attribution%20%28ODC--By%29-lightblue.svg)](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/by/) L00011: L00012: Dataset and code for ["BLADE: Benchmarking Language Model Agents for Data-Driven Science"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.09667) L00013: L00014: We are working on a hold-out test set. Details soon! L00015: L00016: ## 📝 Introduction L00017: L00018: BLADE is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate Language Model (LM) Agents on writing justifiable analyses on real-world scientific research questions from data (e.g., _Are soccer players with a dark skin tone more likely than those with a light skin tone to receive red cards from referees?_ from [Silberzahn et al.](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2515245917747646)). In particular, BLADE evaluates Agents' ability to iteratively integrate scientific domain knowledge, statistical expertise, and data understanding to make nuanced analytical decisions L00019: L00020: BLADE consists of X dataset and research question pairs with high-quality ground truth analysis decisions (i.e., choice of conceptual construct, transformations, statistical model) made by expert data scientists and researchers who independently conducted the analyses. In addition, BLADE contains Y multiple choice questions for discerning justifiable analysis decisions. L00021: L00022: ![Main](https://github.com/behavioral-data/BLADE/raw/main/assets/main_white.png) L00023: L00024:

L00025: Overview of BLADE Construction and Evaluation. We gathered research questions and datasets from existing research papers, crowd-sourced analysis studies and statistic textbooks as well as analyses from expert annotators (boxes 1-3). Given a research question and dataset, LM agents generate a full analysis containing the relevant conceptual variables, a data transform function, and a statistical modeling function (boxes 1, 4, and 5). BLADE then performs automatic evaluation against the ground truth (box 6). L00026:

L00027: L00028: ## 🚀 Getting Started L00029: L00030: To get started with BLADE, follow the steps below: L00031: L00032: ### 1. Installation L00033: L00034: ```bash L00035: # recommended to do this inside another environment L00036: conda create --name blade python=3.10 -y L00037: conda activate blade L00038: pip install blade-bench L00039: ``` L00040: L00041: Or to install locally (developed in python=3.10.14): L00042: L00043: ```bash L00044: # Clone the repository L00045: git clone https://github.com/behavioral-data/BLADE.git L00046: cd BLADE L00047: # install locally L00048: pip install -e . L00049: ``` L00050: L00051: ### 2. LM Setup L00052: L00053: Next, set the API keys for different LM services. BLADE both not only evalutes Language Models but needs one for evaluation. L00054: L00055: ```bash L00056: # for openai L00057: export OPENAI_API_KEY= L00058: L00059: # for google gemini L00060: export GEMINI_API_KEY= L00061: L00062: # for anthropic L00063: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= L00064: ``` L00065: L00066: Some default model configurations (e.g., environment variable for the api key) are specified in [llm_config.yml](blade_bench/conf/llm_config.yml). You can also set your own configurations by creating your own yaml file folloing the format in `llm_config.yml` and setting the environment variable `LLM_CONFIG_PATH` to the file. L00067: L00068: Here's a minimal example to test that the llm is working. L00069: L00070: ```python L00071: from blade_bench.llms import llm L00072: gen = llm(provider="anthropic", model="claude-3.5-sonnet") L00073: response = gen.generate([{"role": "user", "content": "Hello world"}]) L00074: ``` L00075: L00076: ### 3. Running LMs and Agent L00077: L00078: We provide a starter script to run a basic one shot LM or ReACT agent for our benchmark. L00079: L00080: ``` L00081: Usage: run_gen_analyses.py [OPTIONS] L00082: L00083: For a given dataset and research question, generate analyses for the dataset L00084: using a language model or a basic ReAct agent that interacts with a notebook L00085: environment. L00086: L00087: Running this generates the following files in output_dir: L00088: L00089: - command.sh: A bash script that contains the command used to run this script L00090: - config.json: The configuration used to run this experiment L00091: - run.log: The log file for the multirun experiment L00092: - llm.log: The log file for LM prompts and responses for the experiment L00093: - multirun_analyses.json: The analyses generated. **Note**: This file is used in run_get_eval.py to get the evaluation results. L00094: - llm_analysis_*.py: The code generated for each run (if it was generated properly) for quick reference L00095: L00096: Options: L00097: --run_dataset [fish|boxes|conversation|reading|crofoot|panda_nuts|fertility|hurricane|teachingratings|mortgage|soccer|affairs|amtl|caschools] L00098: Dataset to run [required] L00099: -n, --num_runs INTEGER Number of runs to perform [default: 10] L00100: --use_agent Whether to use agent or just the base LM L00101: --no_cache_code_results [ONLY used when use_agent=True] Whether to L00102: --no_cache_code_results [ONLY used when use_agent=True] Whether to L00103: cache code results when running code. L00104: --no_use_data_desc Whether to use data description in the L00105: prompts for the LM [default: True] L00106: --llm_config_path FILE Path to the LLM config file, used to specify L00107: the provider, model, and text generation L00108: config such as the temperature. [default: L00109: ./conf/llm.yaml] L00110: --llm_provider [openai|azureopenai|groq|mistral|together|gemini|anthropic|huggingface] L00111: Provider for the LLM to override the config L00112: file at llm_config_path L00113: --llm_model TEXT Model for the LLM to override the config L00114: file at llm_config_path. L00115: --llm_eval_config_path FILE Path to the LLM eval config file, used to L00116: specify the provider, model, and text L00117: generation config such as the temperature. L00118: [default: ./conf/llm_eval.yaml] L00119: --output_dir DIRECTORY output directory to store saved analyses L00120: --help Show this message and exit. L00121: ``` L00122: L00123: This will write the results to the folder specified by `output_dir`. After running the script, in the output folder, there will be a `multirun_analyses.json` file which is used for evaluation. L00124: L00125: An example is provided in [example/multirun_analyses.json](example/multirun_analyses.json). L00126: L00127: ### 4. Evaluating Agent Generated Analyses L00128: L00129: We provide a starter script to evaluate the outputs of `run_gen_analyses.py`. Run `run_get_eval.py` as follows: L00130: L00131: ``` L00132: Usage: run_get_eval.py [OPTIONS] L00133: L00134: Runs evaluation and saves the results to the output_dir directory. Running L00135: this saves the following key files: L00136: L00137: - command.sh: A bash script that contains the command used to run this script L00138: - eval_results.json of the EvalResults class L00139: - eval_metrics.json of the MetricsAcrossRuns class containing the metrics L00140: - llm_history.json of the LLM history class containing the prompt history L00141: L00142: Options: L00143: --multirun_load_path FILE [EITHER multirun_load_path or L00144: submission_load_path is REQUIRED] Path to L00145: load the multirun analyses. L00146: --submission_load_path FILE [EITHER multirun_load_path or L00147: submission_load_path is REQUIRED] L00148: --llm_eval_config_path FILE Path to the LLM eval config file L00149: --no_cache_code_results Whether to not cache code results when L00150: running code for the evaluation L00151: --output_dir DIRECTORY output directory to store saved eval results L00152: --ks TEXT List of k values for diversity metrics. L00153: Default is [] L00154: --diversity_n_samples INTEGER Number of samples to use for diversity L00155: metrics L00156: --help Show this message and exit. L00157: ``` L00158: L00159: Here is an example: L00160: L00161: ```bash L00162: python run_get_eval.py --multirun_load_path ./examples/multirun_analyses.json L00163: ``` L00164: L00165: ## 🔍 Data Exploration Functions L00166: L00167: To access the dataset and research question we can: L00168: L00169: ```python L00170: from blade_bench.data import load_dataset_info, list_datasets, DatasetInfo L00171: L00172: all_datasets = list_datasets() L00173: dinfo: DatasetInfo = load_dataset_info("soccer", load_df=True) L00174: rq = dinfo.research_question L00175: df = dinfo.df L00176: ``` L00177: L00178: To explore the ground truth annotations, we can: L00179: L00180: ```python L00181: from blade_bench.data import load_ground_truth, AnnotationDBData L00182: L00183: # each dataset annotations will be prepared when it is run the first time L00184: gnd_truth: AnnotationDBData = load_ground_truth('soccer') L00185: print(len(gnd_truth.transform_specs)) L00186: print(len(gnd_truth.cv_specs)) L00187: ``` L00188: L00189: More details about the structure of the ground truth is available in the paper. L00190: L00191: ## 🎯 Evaluating a Submission on BLADE L00192: L00193: To evalute your own agent analysis for a dataset in BLADE, the LM agent must generate a `json` file that conforms to the schema in [example/submission_schema.json](example/submission_schema.json). An example is shown in [example/submission_analyses.json](example/submission_analyses.json). Then, we just need to specify --submission_load_path when running `run_get_eval.py`. L00194: L00195: ```bash L00196: python run_get_eval.py --submission_load_path ./example/submission_analyses.json L00197: ``` L00198: L00199: ## Citation L00200: L00201: If you use our dataset or models in your research, please cite us as follows: L00202: L00203: ```bibtex L00204: @article{gu2024bladebenchmarkinglanguagemodel, L00205: title={BLADE: Benchmarking Language Model Agents for Data-Driven Science}, L00206: author={Ken Gu and Ruoxi Shang and Ruien Jiang and Keying Kuang and Richard-John Lin and Donghe Lyu and Yue Mao and Youran Pan and Teng Wu and Jiaqian Yu and Yikun Zhang and Tianmai M. Zhang and Lanyi Zhu and Mike A. Merrill and Jeffrey Heer and Tim Althoff}, L00207: year={2024}, L00208: journal = {arXiv}, L00209: url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.09667}, L00210: } L00211: ``` L00212: L00213: ## License L00214: L00215: ### Code License L00216: L00217: The code in this repository is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). L00090:         self, llm_config: GenConfig, llm_history: LLMHistory, text_gen: TextGenerator
L00091:     ):

L00094:         if text_gen is not None:
L00095:             self.code_to_transform_llm = CodeToTransformsLLM(

L00101:     async def convert_entire_analysis(
L00102:         self, entire_analysis: EntireAnalysis
L00103:     ) -> Tuple[EntireAnalysisProcessed, Union[None, EvalRunResults]]:
L00104:         try:
L00105:             state_data: Union[TransformDatasetState] = (
L00106:                 await self.get_state_data_from_code(
L00107:                     entire_analysis.transform_code_inside_func
L00108:                 )
L00109:             )
L00110:             run_results = None
L00111:         except RunError as e:
L00112:             state_data = None
L00113:             run_results = EvalRunResults(
L00114:                 info=e.message,
L00115:                 res_type=e.res_type,
L00116:             )
L00117: 
L00118:         model_code: ModelAndColumns = self.code_to_model_llm.code_to_model_obj(
L00119:             entire_analysis.model_code_inside_func
L00120:         )
L00121:         cvar_specs = entire_analysis.cvars.to_cvar_specs()
L00122:         model_spec = model_code.to_model_spec()
L00123: 
L00124:         analysis = EntireAnalysisProcessed(
L00125:             cv_specs=cvar_specs,
L00126:             m_specs={model_spec.spec_id: model_spec},
L00127:             transform_state=state_data,
L00128:             agent_cvars=entire_analysis.cvars,
L00129:             m_code_and_cols=model_code,
L00130:         )
L00131:         return analysis, run_results

L00133:     async def get_transform_state_with_cache(
L00134:         self, transform_ret: List[TransformDataReturn]
L00135:     ):
L00136:         inp = {
L00137:             "codes": [ts.code for ts in transform_ret],
L00138:             "tverbs": [ts.transform_verb for ts in transform_ret],
L00139:             "col_mappings": [
L00140:                 {
L00141:                     str(tuple(sorted(key))): value
L00142:                     for key, value in ts.column_mapping.items()
L00143:                 }
L00144:                 for ts in transform_ret
L00145:             ],
L00146:             "groupby_cols": [
L00147:                 str(tuple(sorted(ts.groupby_cols))) for ts in transform_ret
L00148:             ],
L00149:             "dataset": self.run_dataset,
L00150:         }
L00151: 
L00152:         logger.bind(message=json.dumps(inp, indent=2)).log(
L00153:             TS_STATE_QUERY, "Getting transform state"
L00154:         )
L00155:         if self.use_code_cache:
L00156:             start_time = time.time()
L00157:             state_data: TransformDatasetState = cache_request(self.cache, params=inp)
L00158:             if state_data:
L00159:                 logger.bind(
L00160:                     from_cache=True,
L00161:                     cache_elapsed_time=time.time() - start_time,
L00162:                     message=json.dumps(state_data.summary_dict, indent=2),
L00163:                 ).log(TS_STATE_RESP, "Finished getting transform state")
L00164:                 return state_data
L00165:         start_time = time.time()
L00166:         state_data = await self.annotation.build_state_data_from_transform_return(
L00167:             transform_ret
L00168:         )
L00169:         elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time
L00170:         logger.bind(
L00171:             from_cache=False,
L00172:             api_elapsed_time=elapsed_time,
L00173:             message=json.dumps(state_data.summary_dict, indent=2),
L00174:         ).log(TS_STATE_RESP, "Finished getting transform state")
L00175:         cache_request(self.cache, params=inp, values=state_data)
L00176: 
L00177:         return state_data

L00179:     async def run_code_with_cache(
L00180:         self, code: str, executor: Literal["code_executor", "transform_executor"]
L00181:     ) -> ExecutorReturn:
L00182:         inp = {
L00183:             "executor": executor,
L00184:             "code": code,
L00185:             "dataset": self.run_dataset,
L00186:         }
L00187:         logger.bind(message=code).log(CODE_ENV_QUERY, f"Running code with {executor}")
L00188:         if self.use_code_cache:
L00189:             start_time = time.time()
L00190:             code_res: ExecutorReturn = cache_request(self.cache, params=inp)
L00191:             if code_res:
L00192:                 logger.bind(
L00193:                     from_cache=True,
L00194:                     message=(
L00195:                         f"[Success]\n" + code_res.output
L00196:                         if code_res.success
L00197:                         else "[Error]\n" + code_res.output
L00198:                     ),
L00199:                     cache_elapsed_time=time.time() - start_time,
L00200:                 ).log(CODE_ENV_RESP, f"Finished running code with {executor}")
L00201:                 return code_res
L00202:         start_time = time.time()
L00203:         if executor == "code_executor":
L00204:             code_res = await self.code_executor.run_code(code)
L00205:         elif executor == "transform_executor":
L00206:             code_res = await self.transform_executor.run_code(code)
L00207: 
L00208:         elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time
L00209:         logger.bind(
L00210:             from_cache=False,
L00211:             api_elapsed_time=elapsed_time,
L00212:             message=(
L00213:                 f"[Success]\n" + code_res.output
L00214:                 if code_res.success
L00215:                 else "[Error]\n" + code_res.output
L00216:             ),
L00217:         ).log(CODE_ENV_RESP, f"Finished running code with {executor}")
L00218:         cache_request(self.cache, params=inp, values=code_res)
L00219:         return code_res

L00221:     async def get_state_data_from_code(
L00222:         self, code, max_retries: int = 3
L00223:     ) -> Union[TransformDatasetState, EvalRunResults]:
L00224:         try:
L00225:             ast.parse(code)
L00226:         except Exception as e:
L00227:             raise LMSubmissionExecutionError(
L00228:                 message=f"Code has syntax error, cannot parse with AST: {e}",
L00229:                 res_type=RunResultModes.LM_SUBMISSION_EXECUTION_FAILED,
L00230:             )
L00231: 
L00232:         code_res: ExecutorReturn = await self.run_code_with_cache(code, "code_executor")
L00233:         if not code_res.success:
L00234:             raise LMSubmissionExecutionError(
L00235:                 message=code_res.output,
L00236:                 res_type=RunResultModes.LM_SUBMISSION_EXECUTION_FAILED,
L00237:             )
L00238: 
L00239:         if not astor.to_source(ast.parse(code)):
L00240:             raise LMSubmissionEmptyError(
L00241:                 message="Code is empty after parsing",
L00242:                 res_type=RunResultModes.LM_SUBMISSION_TRANSFORM_CODE_EMPTY,
L00243:             )
L00244: 
L00245:         retries = 0
L00246:         converted_code = self.code_to_transform_llm.convert_code(code)
L00247:         while retries < max_retries:
L00248:             code_res: ExecutorReturn = await self.run_code_with_cache(
L00249:                 converted_code, "transform_executor"
L00250:             )
L00251:             if code_res.success:
L00252:                 break
L00253:             else:
L00254:                 retries += 1
L00255:                 if retries < max_retries:
L00256:                     logger.warning(f"Code conversion failed, retrying")
L00257:                     background_code = self.transform_executor.init_code.format(
L00258:                         data_path="data.csv"
L00259:                     )
L00260:                     postfix_code = self.transform_executor.postfix_code.format(
L00261:                         save_path="save_path.pkl"
L00262:                     )
L00263:                     _, function_names = extract_code_inside_functions_and_func_names(
L00264:                         converted_code
L00265:                     )
L00266:                     code_and_reflection = self.debug_llm.debug_code(
L00267:                         background_code=background_code,
L00268:                         function_code=converted_code,
L00269:                         curr_code=postfix_code,
L00270:                         runtime_error=code_res.output,
L00271:                         func_names=function_names,
L00272:                     )
L00273:                     converted_code = code_and_reflection.code
L00274:                 else:
L00275:                     logger.error(f"Code conversion failed after {max_retries} retries")
L00276:         if not code_res.success:
L00277:             raise LMSubmissionExecutionError(
L00278:                 message=f"Code conversion failed after {max_retries} retries\n{code_res.output}",
L00279:                 res_type=RunResultModes.LM_SUBMISSION_CONVERSION_FAILED,
L00280:             )
L00281: 
L00282:         transform_ret: List[TransformDataReturn] = code_res.value
L00283:         codes, _ = extract_code_inside_functions_and_func_names(converted_code)
L00284:         for i, ts in enumerate(transform_ret):
L00285:             ts.code = codes[i]
L00286:         if not transform_ret:
L00287:             raise LMSubmissionExecutionError(
L00288:                 message="No transforms were returned",
